findings.fix_direction: Add a check:skips step to the quality job; reconcile BASELINE to current real per-platform counts once, then let the existing monotonic-ratchet design (already correct) do its job going forward.

verification.evidence:
The main claim holds, and I checked it in the code. Some details and the severity are off.

1) The gate is never run. package.json:80 defines "check:skips": "node scripts/check-skipped-tests.mjs". Grepping .github/, scripts/ and package.json finds no caller. The quality job runs typecheck, check:bugs, build and npm test (.github/workflows/build.yml:42-56). release.yml:42-49 is the same. The "test" script at package.json:33 does not chain it either. The script's own header says a newly skipped test "fails the build" (check-skipped-tests.mjs:17-18). That is false, because nothing in the build calls it.

2) The baseline is stale, which I proved by running the gate. BASELINE={win32:12,darwin:1,linux:18} is at scripts/check-skipped-tests.mjs:79. I ran it read-only against the existing receipt metis-2.0-exec/receipts/baseline-desktop.json (sha 2bf21f1c, macOS, numPendingTests 25). It exits 1 with 10 problems:
- 25 skipped tests against a darwin baseline of 1
- 9 skipped tests with no declared reason, from 3 test files that have no REASONS entry:
  - scripts/mac-helper-privacy.test.ts (added 2026-09-23 in 5c521826)
  - scripts/verify-signing.test.ts (runIf win32, added 2026-09-12 in b39cf218)
  - src/renderer/src/components/OnboardingExperience.browser.test.ts (skipIf ASKTOTO_BROWSER_QA!=='1', added 2026-09-22 in fca1e6b5)

The gate script was last changed on 2026-08-29 (91c32600). docs/qa/QA-APPROVAL-REBUILD-2026-08-29.md records a manual "PASS — linux baseline 18". Every skip added after that date got in without being caught. This is exactly the failure the finding predicts, and it has already happened.

3) Where the finding is wrong:
- The CI quality matrix is ubuntu-latest and windows-latest only (build.yml:32-33). No macOS runner exists, so the darwin baseline would not be checked even if the step were added. The baselines CI would check are linux:18 and win32:12.
- The "~25x" darwin gap depends on the machine. The receipt came from a clean Mac with no mac-helper or llama-server binaries (see the local-runtime skip title: "missing: mac binary ..."). So mac-helper, apple-speech and local-runtime skip there but would not on a fully set-up dev Mac.
- The problem that does not depend on the machine is the missing REASONS entries. The Onboarding browser test (6 tests) skips on every CI OS. verify-signing and mac-helper-privacy skip on linux. So the gate would fail on BOTH matrix legs on its first run.
- Linux count, estimated by reading the skip conditions (not observed on a Linux machine): about 27-30, against a baseline of 18.

4) Severity is P2, not P1. This is a gap in CI quality with no effect on the running app. It does not cause or explain E1-E9 or Tony's two bug reports (heaviness, History freeze). One side note: the llama-server spawn test (local-runtime.test.ts:270) and the MQA-338 regression pin (OnboardingExperience.browser.test.ts) never run in CI. So sidecar lifecycle is not tested in CI, but this finding does not cause that.
verification.corrected_mechanism_or_fix:
How it actually fails: check:skips is not called from any workflow or from npm test. Since it was last updated (2026-08-29), 3 new skipped test files arrived with no declared reason (Sep 12, 22 and 23). The gate now fails on every platform: darwin as observed, linux and win32 by reading the skip conditions. So the 'declare every skip' rule has already stopped holding. The darwin baseline does not matter to CI, because CI has no macOS leg.

Fix, in order:
1. In the build.yml quality job (ubuntu and windows), don't let the script start a second vitest run (lines 90-101 run the full suite again). Have the main suite run write a JSON report: `vitest run --reporter=default --reporter=json --outputFile=vitest-report.json`. Then run `node scripts/check-skipped-tests.mjs vitest-report.json`, or add that call to the end of npm test.
2. Add REASONS entries for mac-helper-privacy.test.ts, verify-signing.test.ts and OnboardingExperience.browser.test.ts. For the browser test, a better option is to set ASKTOTO_BROWSER_QA=1 in the quality job, since Playwright Chromium is already installed at build.yml:54-55. The MQA-338 pin would then actually run instead of being declared skipped.
3. Set BASELINE.linux and BASELINE.win32 from the first real CI report. After that, the existing ratchet only lets the numbers go down.
4. For darwin, either add a macos-latest quality leg or state that the darwin baseline assumes a Mac with the build artifacts provisioned (mac-helper, llama-server, GGUF). Without that, its count changes with whatever is installed on the machine and is not a stable number to enforce.

findings.title: docs/**.md (60+ files) is exempt from both secret-scanning mechanisms
findings.evidence: .gitleaks.toml:41 allowlists '^docs/.*\.md$' repo-wide; build.yml's narrow secret-scan step (lines 159-167) roots on src/scripts/build/intelligence/src/.github + named config files only, and its --include list (*.ts/*.tsx/*.js/*.mjs/*.json/*.yml) never includes .md anyway.
findings.failure_scenario: An engineer pastes a real API key into a runbook (e.g. docs/operator/RUNBOOKS.md) while documenting a debug session; it ships to the public repo with zero CI secret-scan coverage from either mechanism.
findings.fix_direction: Narrow the gitleaks allowlist to specific, tagged fake-fixture paths (as the other 4 allowlisted cases already are) instead of blanket-exempting the whole docs/ tree.

verification.evidence:
I read the code myself and it works the way the finding says. The severity is too high: the docs exemption hides nothing today, and a leak would need someone to make a mistake first, so this is a defense-in-depth gap in CI and not an active exposure.

What I read:
- .gitleaks.toml:40-41 does allowlist '''^docs/.*\.md$''' by path, across the whole repo, with the comment "Documentation examples ... never live keys". There are 81 .md files under docs/ (`find docs -name '*.md' | wc -l`), more than the finding's "60+".
- .github/workflows/build.yml:159-169 is the narrow "Secret scan" step. It only greps `src scripts build intelligence/src .github` plus the electron-builder*.yml files and package.json. Its --include list is *.ts/*.tsx/*.js/*.mjs/*.json/*.yml, so neither docs/ nor any .md file is ever scanned. That also leaves out README.md at the repo root and other .md files outside docs/, though gitleaks does still cover those.
- build.yml:191-195 is the gitleaks step, pinned to v8.30.1 by digest. It runs `detect --source=/repo --config=/repo/.gitleaks.toml` on a shallow depth-1 checkout, so the docs path allowlist applies there too. The security job runs on every branch push and on PRs to main (build.yml:10-18), and build-macos and build-windows need it (build.yml:213, 362). So the mechanism can be reached in the production pipeline.
- The header comment (.gitleaks.toml:15-25) lists the 5 real false positives from the baseline history scan. None of them is in docs/. The docs entry was added on speculation, not to silence an actual hit.

Tests I ran locally with gitleaks 8.30.1, redacted, repo not modified:
- I removed only the docs entry into a scratch copy of the config. `gitleaks dir docs` then gave 0 findings.
- `gitleaks git .` over the full history (78.76 MB) with that config gave 0 findings under docs/. So the docs exemption currently hides nothing, and removing it would not turn CI red.
- A grep with the narrow-scan regex over docs/ finds key-shaped strings in docs/WINDOWS.md:148 and docs/qa/BUG-LEDGER.md:2521, 3687 and 3699, all with the sk-kimi-/sk-proj-/sk-or- prefixes. From their context they are placeholder or probe strings in QA write-ups. BUG-LEDGER.md:3687 is a random-looking 25-character leak-probe value, which I did not print. None of them trips the gitleaks default rules. They do show the finding's scenario is realistic: engineers already paste key-shaped strings into docs/qa ledgers, and neither gate looks at them.

Why P2 and not P1:
- It needs a human to make an error first, and nothing is leaked today.
- It has nothing to do with the heaviness or freeze/crash that Tony reported.
- I could not check whether the repo is public or whether GitHub push protection is turned on. `gh` failed in the sandbox with a TLS error, so the finding's "public repo" claim is unconfirmed.

Side note, not part of this finding: a history-only gitleaks scan with the docs entry removed flagged one `private-key` hit at operator/src/test-fixtures.ts:7 in commit 33c06a29 (2026-08-31). It is not covered by the allowlist, because that file does not match *.test.ts. The file at HEAD no longer contains a PEM block (its header now says keypairs are generated at runtime), so CI's shallow scan of HEAD will not trip on it. It is still in history, though, which contradicts the 2026-08-21 "clean full-history baseline" claim.
verification.corrected_mechanism_or_fix:
The mechanism is correct as stated. The docs path allowlist in .gitleaks.toml (lines 40-41) turns off gitleaks for all 81 docs/**/*.md files. The narrow grep scan in build.yml (lines 159-167) never covers docs/ or any *.md file. Together, nothing scans the documentation at all.

Fix: delete the '''^docs/.*\.md$''' entry and its comment on line 40, which also means removing the trailing comma after '''^scripts/qa/.*'''. I checked locally that this adds 0 findings, both on the current tree and across the full history. If a future doc example ever trips a rule, handle it narrowly: put an inline `gitleaks:allow` comment on that line, or add a regex/stopwords allowlist for obvious placeholders (x{4,}, "example", "<your-key>"). Do not bring back a path-wide exemption.

Optional: add --include='*.md' and the docs root to the narrow build.yml scan so the product-specific sk-kimi- shape is caught in runbooks too. If you do, first redact or tag the existing probe strings in docs/qa/BUG-LEDGER.md (lines 2521, 3687, 3699) and docs/WINDOWS.md:148. Also update the comment in .gitleaks.toml (lines 27-29): it claims the allowlist mirrors the narrow scan's exclusions, and for docs that is not true.

Adjusted severity: P2, a CI hardening gap with no current leak.

- `grep -l "readFileSync(join(__dirname, 'index.ts')"` matches 37 of the 51 `src/main/*.contract.test.ts` files (the finding said 36), and 44 contract files mention index.ts in some form.

Its only test is security-audit-10.contract.test.ts:209-217, which regex-matches the body text (`/if \(!win \|\| win\.isDestroyed\(\)\)/`, the `noteIpcDenied(...)` strings). An inserted early `return` at the top would keep every match green, so the "silent bypass stays green" part holds.

The code itself confirms the "brittle pins warp the code" half of the claim. index.ts:4164-4168 (stopSidecarsForHardExit) reads: "Deliberately a copy rather than a shared helper — several source-contract tests pin these exact calls inside the `will-quit` handler body". So the source pins have already forced the sidecar teardown (localRuntime.stop, fmRuntime.stop, screenPreprocess.stop) to be duplicated instead of shared. That is the path behind the orphaned llama-server processes in E2, and it can only be source-pinned, not behavior-tested.

A precedent for the fix already exists. src/main/listening-state-ipc.ts:18 exports `createListeningStateHandler({assertMainWindow, requireAuth, ...sideEffects})`, and security-audit-10.contract.test.ts:41-58 tests it by behavior with `vi.fn()` spies (`expect(assertMainWindow).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)`).

findings.title: Desktop app's integration-kind allowlist has drifted from the Worker's connector catalog, silently dropping supported integrations
findings.evidence: src/shared/operator-entitlements.ts:166-173 defines OPERATOR_INTEGRATION_KINDS as a hand-maintained 7-entry list (hubspot, salesforce, pipedrive, clickup, plane, notion, custom-mcp), used at line 192 (parseOperatorIntegration) to validate GET /v1/integrations responses. src/shared/operator-connectors.ts:32 defines CONNECTOR_KINDS as a 28-entry list (adds zoho, dynamics365, attio, close, jira, linear, asana, monday, trello, airtable, zendesk, intercom, freshdesk, confluence, sharepoint, googledrive, github, gitlab, slack, microsoftteams, custom-rest). operator/src/connectors/catalog.ts:14 imports CONNECTOR_KINDS from operator-connectors.ts (the Worker DID adopt the shared source), but operator-entitlements.ts does not import it at all (grep confirmed zero references). The file's own doc comment (operator-connectors.ts:1-8) says the desktop entitlement layer 'is meant to derive its own kind list from CONNECTOR_KINDS so the two lists cannot drift (DT1, later)' -- the string 'DT1' appears exactly once in the whole repo, i.e. this was never done.
findings.failure_scenario: A user connects any of the 21 integration kinds present in CONNECTOR_KINDS but absent from OPERATOR_INTEGRATION_KINDS (e.g. jira, slack, github, linear, zendesk -- all live in the Worker's catalog today). parseOperatorIntegration at operator-entitlements.ts:192 returns null for that entry because INTEGRATION_KIND_SET.has(o.kind) fails, so the integration is silently dropped from the desktop app's parsed list with no error surfaced -- indistinguishable from malformed input, even though it's a real, Worker-supported integration the user just connected.
findings.fix_direction: Delete OPERATOR_INTEGRATION_KINDS/INTEGRATION_KIND_SET from operator-entitlements.ts; import CONNECTOR_KINDS (or a ConnectorKind-derived set) from operator-connectors.ts instead, exactly as the existing doc comment prescribes. Single-file change, can only widen accepted kinds to match what the Worker already sends, low risk, closes a live bug today.

verification.evidence:
The drift is real and the line numbers are right. The finding overstates the impact and the severity, and the proposed fix is incomplete.

What I confirmed in the code:
- src/shared/operator-entitlements.ts:166-173 has a hand-kept list of 7 kinds (OPERATOR_INTEGRATION_KINDS). Line 177 builds INTEGRATION_KIND_SET from it, and line 192 in parseOperatorIntegration returns null for any kind outside that set.
- src/shared/operator-connectors.ts:32-61 lists 28 kinds in CONNECTOR_KINDS. Its doc comment (lines 4-6) says the desktop list should be derived from it ("DT1, later"). A grep shows operator-entitlements.ts never imports it. Only the Worker side uses it (catalog.ts:14, logo-slugs.ts:17).
- The Worker sends the admin-chosen kind unchanged. operator/src/routes/integrations.ts:230-270 accepts any catalog kind when an admin creates an integration, with mode 'direct' or 'brokered' (brokered is the default). operator/src/routes/integrations-seat.ts:225-256 delivers `kind: row.kind` for both shapes.
- I ran the real parser with bun on a payload shaped like the Worker's response. A direct github row (baseUrl https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/ plus a credential) and a brokered jira row were both dropped. Result: [["b","custom-mcp",...,true],["d","hubspot",null,false]].
- So the silent drop is confirmed. The rows vanish from `integrations` in the operator-status IPC (src/main/index.ts:5206) and from the MCP registry that Settings reads (index.ts:5213, Settings.tsx:8056).

Why the impact is overstated:
1. Only seats with an Operator URL and secret configured are affected (operatorGate and useConnection in operator-integrations.ts:155). An Operator admin creates these integrations, not the end user. None of this connects to Tony's heaviness or History-freeze reports, or to the runtime evidence E1-E9.
2. Brokered is the Worker's default mode (data.ts:39,55; integrations.ts:270). The desktop parser reads only baseUrl and credential, and nothing under src/ reads `endpoint` or `gatewayToken`. A brokered row of any kind, including the 7 allowed ones, therefore parses with baseUrl and credential set to null. reconcileOperatorMcpRegistry (operator-integrations.ts:82) then skips it. In the probe, the brokered hubspot row survived but had nothing to connect to. The kind list only matters for direct-mode rows.
3. The desktop's only way to use an integration is the generic bearer MCP client (connectMcp, operator-integrations.ts:128), plus the CRM credential swap, which covers 'plane' only (line 301). Every catalog kind uses REST transport except github and custom-mcp (operator-connectors.ts:317-321, 357-361). So jira, slack, linear, zendesk and the other REST kinds would fail tool discovery even if they were accepted. The one real functional loss is a direct-mode github connection: a working MCP server the admin set up that never appears on the seat. The other kinds are only missing from the Settings list.
4. P0 is not justified: no crash, no data loss, no security exposure. This is a silent feature gap in an enterprise admin-managed path, so P2 fits.
verification.corrected_mechanism_or_fix:
Mechanism: the desktop's handling of the GET /v1/integrations response has drifted from the Worker in two ways, and the kind list is only one of them.
(a) The kind allowlist (operator-entitlements.ts:166-177, checked at :192) drops direct or brokered rows of the 21 kinds it does not list.
(b) The parser ignores the brokered response shape (mode, transport, endpoint, gatewayToken). Brokered is the Worker's default, so brokered rows of every kind reach the desktop with no baseUrl or credential and are never registered.

Fix:
1. In operator-entitlements.ts, delete OPERATOR_INTEGRATION_KINDS and INTEGRATION_KIND_SET. Replace the check at line 192 with isConnectorKind(o.kind) from @shared/operator-connectors, and make OperatorIntegrationKind an alias of ConnectorKind. Every use in src/main/operator-integrations.ts (:22, :54, :260, :301, :315) still compiles because the new type is a superset.
2. Do not widen the list on its own. reconcileOperatorMcpRegistry (operator-integrations.ts:82) registers every direct row with a baseUrl as an MCP server, so widening would add REST-transport kinds (jira, slack and others) that fail discovery through connectMcp. Gate registration on CONNECTOR_CATALOG_CORE[it.kind].transport === 'mcp'. That also fixes the existing mis-registration of direct hubspot, pipedrive and other REST rows.
3. Separately, parse and use the brokered shape. Either call the Worker gateway at `${operatorUrl}${endpoint}` with gatewayToken as the bearer, or show brokered rows as "managed, not usable on this device yet". Without this, the default-mode integrations stay dead on the desktop whatever the kind list says.
4. Add a test that keeps the desktop parser's accepted kinds equal to CONNECTOR_KINDS, and one for the brokered row shape. The current test at operator-entitlements.test.ts:184 only covers 'not-a-real-kind'.

verification.evidence:
I checked every factual claim against /Users/<redacted-user>/AI-Brain-build/metis-2.0 at HEAD 2bf21f1c. All of them hold.

- **Size:** `wc -l src/main/index.ts` gives 9,518 lines. The finding's 9,519 is off by one, which doesn't matter.
- **IPC handlers:** `grep -cE 'ipcMain\.(handle|on)'` gives 168, and index.ts is the only non-test file under src/main that registers any. They all sit inside one function, `registerIpc()`, which runs from L4624 to about L8771. That single function is roughly 4,150 lines.
- **Fan-out:** there are 135 distinct internal import specifiers: 112 relative plus 23 `@shared/*`. The next highest file is src/renderer/src/App.tsx with 49, then Settings.tsx with 39. That is about 2.75x, not ~2.4x, so the finding understates it.
- **Shared state:** module scope holds 53 top-level `let` and 143 top-level functions.
- **Cited lines are exact:**
  - `getSpeakerId` L254 and `cleanupExpiredLiveSpeakerReceipts` L289.
  - Import-speaker state machine L399-436 (`beginImportSpeakers`, `captureImportSpeakerKey`, `finalizeImportSpeakers`, `disposeImportSpeakers`).
  - `makeRefreshDustAuth` L841.
  - `contentProtectionOn` and `privateViewOn` L966-979.
  - Cloud-STT owner arbitration L1051-1064 (`isCurrentCloudSttOwner`, `invalidateCloudSttOwner`).
  - `noteIpcDenied` L1147, `assertMainWindow` L1154, `isMainWindowSender` L1172, `denyIfLimited` L1189, `assertBrainReader` L1201.
- **The gate depends on file globals:** it reads the module-level `let win` directly (declared at L981) and is applied by hand in each handler. `assertMainWindow(` appears 155 times in the file.
- **Supporting evidence the finding missed:** src/main/index-audit-fixes.contract.test.ts L5-7 says index.ts starts Electron as soon as it is imported, so there is no index.test.ts. About 71 test files instead read index.ts as raw text (`readFileSync(join(__dirname,'index.ts'))`) and slice it between string markers (e.g. L20-29). So the IPC security gate can only be checked by matching source text, not by running it.

**Why PARTIAL and not CONFIRMED:**

1. **Severity is too high.** This is maintainability debt. It is not a defect that users hit. Nothing in the file's size causes the runtime evidence:
   - E2: orphaned llama-server processes.
   - E3/E6: render-process-gone, app.unresponsive, force-quit cycles.
   - E5: the capture retry loop.
   - Tony's "heavy" and "History freezes" reports.

   "Compounds diagnosis difficulty" is an opinion, not a way the app fails. P2 fits better: it matters for the v2.0 "simplify / well-structured" goal, but on its own it breaks nothing.
2. **The fix is harder than "pure move-plus-import-update".** The ~71 tests that slice index.ts by text markers will break when code moves. The security helpers also cannot move as-is, because they close over the `win` global and `isIntelligenceSender`.
verification.corrected_mechanism_or_fix:
Corrected mechanism: this is maintainability and testability debt, not a cause of any runtime symptom. Every IPC handler, including the IPC security gate, lives in one ~4,150-line `registerIpc()` closure (L4624-~8771). The file sits in a 9.5k-line module with 53 mutable module-level `let` values, and it starts Electron as soon as it is imported. As a result nothing in it can be unit-tested. About 71 tests check it by reading index.ts as text and slicing between string markers. That locks in the current layout and cannot prove the security gate works when it runs.

Corrected fix:
1. Create `main/ipc/guards.ts` exporting `createIpcGuards({ getMainWindow, isIntelligenceSender, auditLog, consumeSecurityLimit })`. It returns `assertMainWindow`, `isMainWindowSender`, `assertBrainReader`, `denyIfLimited` and `noteIpcDenied`. Add real behavioral unit tests with fake event, sender and frame objects. In the same PR, retarget the source-scanning tests that check these guards.
2. Split `registerIpc()` into per-feature `register<Feature>Ipc(ctx)` modules, for example speaker-id, import-jobs, dust-auth, cloud-stt and overlay. Pass state in through an explicit context object instead of module globals. Do one feature per PR, and migrate that feature's text-matching contract tests to behavioral tests in the same PR.
3. Keep this as P2 structural work in the v2.0 plan. Do not tie it to the crash, freeze or heaviness evidence (E2-E6), which needs its own root-cause findings: sidecar reaping, the capture retry loop, and renderer-kill handling.

findings.fix_direction: Delete whisper-worklet.ts, or better, convert whisper-worklet-src.ts to use the same .toString()-transplant technique vad.ts already proves out in this exact codebase (whisper-worklet-src.ts already imports makeVad/isSpeechLikeWindow from vad and PCM_16K_RESAMPLER_SRC from pcm-format using this pattern).

findings.title: shared/ipc.ts is a 2,408-line undivided IPC contract with the highest fan-in in the repo (87 importers)
findings.evidence: wc -l -> 2,408. Fan-in 87, highest of any file scanned. Consumed by main, preload and renderer alike as the single IPC type/channel surface.
findings.failure_scenario: Any cross-process IPC change touches this one file regardless of feature area, so unrelated feature work across main and renderer collides here in merge conflicts and code review, and the file's size makes any single contract hard to locate or reason about in isolation.
findings.fix_direction: Split into shared/contracts/{brain,ask,listen,overlay,operator,license,import,...}.ts grouped by feature domain, ideally after main/index.ts's feature split (step 6 in the migration plan) so domain boundaries are derived from that work rather than guessed. Optionally keep a thin ipc.ts barrel during migration.

findings.title: src/main, renderer/components, renderer/lib and shared are flat namespaces with no feature grouping
findings.evidence: src/main has 105 non-test .ts files directly at its root plus only 7 partial feature subfolders (brain, cloud-stt, island, license, llm, mcp, net). src/renderer/src/components has 55 flat .tsx files (Settings.tsx 9,378 LOC alongside 23-line Logo.tsx with no subfolder grouping). src/renderer/src/lib has 53 flat files. src/shared has 71 flat files and zero subfolders except test fixtures.
findings.failure_scenario: Infra concerns (secrets.ts, win-security.ts, windows-keystore-dpapi.ts), platform glue (mac-helper.ts) and feature logic (calendar.ts, outlook-write.ts, dust-*.ts) all sit at the same directory level, making it impossible to tell from directory structure alone what's a cross-cutting concern versus a single feature, and same-basename collisions (store.ts, cli.ts, metrics.ts existing twice with unrelated meanings) make fuzzy file search ambiguous.
findings.fix_direction: Adopt the target architecture in the report's section 9: main/{app,windows,ipc,features/*,infra/*}, renderer/{app,features/*,ui/,lib/}, shared/contracts/*, migrating incrementally per the 8-step plan that keeps the app shippable at every commit.

findings.title: Two test files cross the renderer/shared -> main boundary that production code otherwise respects
findings.evidence: src/renderer/src/lib/onboarding-kinetic-grid.test.ts imports src/main/island/geometry.ts directly (../../../main/island/geometry). src/shared/hash.test.ts imports src/main/screen-preprocess.ts directly (../main/screen-preprocess). No production-code layering violations found anywhere else in the scanned graph.
findings.failure_scenario: The two layers are being validated together through a direct import instead of through the IPC contract meant to decouple them, weakening the test suite's ability to catch a real contract break between main and renderer/shared.
findings.fix_direction: If the imported logic (island/geometry.ts's math, screen-preprocess.ts's function) is genuinely shared/pure, move it into src/shared/ and update both the production caller and the test import -- a small, behavior-neutral fix per file.

findings.title: Eleven additional confirmed-dead files from superseded or abandoned work, 1-2 months stale
findings.evidence: Hand-verified (no static or dynamic-load importer) orphans: operator-test-keypair.ts, ControlBar.tsx (superseded 2026-08-31 per commit message 'replace wait chrome with thinking-orbs luxury status'), OnboardingStarfield.tsx, bar-toolbar-layout.ts, Logo.tsx, RecordingIndicator.tsx, shared/brain-analyze.ts (all three from the 2026-07-19 'Mac-side work in progress -- bootstrap' commit), scramble.ts.
findings.failure_scenario: Dead files remain type-checked, lint-checked, and discoverable via search as if live, adding noise to any future audit or refactor and occasionally getting 'fixed' by mistake (same risk class as F5).
findings.fix_direction: Delete after a quick confirm-abandoned pass per file (git history already suggests each was superseded by a specific later commit, e.g. Logo.tsx/RecordingIndicator.tsx by MetisMark.tsx/MantuLogo.tsx branding work).

refactor_opportunities.rationale: The app's actual IPC-authorization boundary (assertMainWindow, denyIfLimited, assertBrainReader, noteIpcDenied) currently lives as free functions inside a 9,519-line file alongside unrelated feature code. Promoting it to its own module makes the security convention explicit and enforceable rather than implicit and easy to forget, and is the single highest-value, lowest-risk first cut into main/index.ts.
refactor_opportunities.target_structure: src/main/ipc/security.ts exporting the four gate functions; every future main/ipc/<channel>.ts handler module imports from it.

The repo already has a working precedent (main/brain/, main/llm/, main/license/, main/cloud-stt/, main/island/, main/net/, main/mcp/ all exist and are reasonably sized) -- this proposal just finishes applying that pattern to what's left flat in index.ts.
refactor_opportunities.target_structure: main/features/{speaker-id,import-jobs,dust-auth,overlay}/ each holding the free functions currently defined inline in index.ts (e.g. getSpeakerId, cleanupExpiredLiveSpeakerReceipts, makeRefreshDustAuth, rememberRetiringOverlaySender), moved feature-by-feature as independently shippable PRs.

refactor_opportunities.rationale: 2,408 lines with 87 importers means every cross-process change touches one file regardless of feature, causing merge contention across unrelated main/renderer work. Splitting after the main/features/* extraction (so domain boundaries are derived, not guessed) minimizes rework.
refactor_opportunities.target_structure: shared/contracts/{brain,ask,listen,overlay,operator,license,import,settings}.ts, optionally re-exported from a thin shared/ipc.ts barrel during migration.

refactor_opportunities.rationale: Section/ToggleRow/ctl are generic UI-kit primitives trapped inside a 9,378-line page component, forcing TapCalibration.tsx to import back from Settings.tsx and creating a real cycle. This is the renderer-side mirror of the ipc/security.ts extraction: small, mechanical, immediately removes a confirmed cycle.
refactor_opportunities.target_structure: src/renderer/src/ui/SettingsPrimitives.tsx (or similar) exporting Section/ToggleRow/ctl; both Settings.tsx and TapCalibration.tsx import from it instead of each other.

refactor_opportunities.title: Unify whisper-worklet duplication using the vad.ts .toString()-transplant pattern
refactor_opportunities.rationale: The codebase already has a proven, documented technique for keeping a typechecked module and its AudioWorklet-string counterpart in sync (vad.ts's makeVad.toString() transplant, explicitly commented as 'zero drift'). whisper-worklet.ts/whisper-worklet-src.ts solve the identical problem but diverged instead, leaving a dead file and an un-typechecked live string.
refactor_opportunities.target_structure: whisper-worklet-src.ts's WHISPER_WORKLET_SRC built from a .toString() transplant of a real, typechecked, tested module (replacing the dead whisper-worklet.ts, or reusing its class if still accurate).

test_gaps: No test appears to isolate main/index.ts's IPC-security gate (assertMainWindow/denyIfLimited/assertBrainReader) as a standalone unit; with the gate embedded in a 9,519-line file sharing module scope with 135 other dependencies, true isolation is structurally implausible regardless of the main area's otherwise strong 1.65 test-to-source ratio -- extracting main/ipc/security.ts (refactor above) is a prerequisite for closing this gap, not just an architecture nicety.

No test catches the OPERATOR_INTEGRATION_KINDS vs CONNECTOR_KINDS drift (F3) -- a parity/fitness-function test asserting the two lists stay in sync (or, after the fix, a single shared source) would prevent recurrence.

preload/ has only 1 test file for 3 source files (0.33 ratio), the thinnest coverage of any area, though preload's low-logic contextBridge-exposure role makes this lower priority than the other gaps here.

No test/lint rule flags an orphaned file (like whisper-worklet.ts or the unwired command-mic feature) -- a periodic import-graph check (the same technique this lane's script uses) run in CI would catch both classes of dead/unwired code before they accumulate further.
